issues.text: Frame 1 (0.0 s) is almost empty: one orange dot and a ghosted card at about 10 percent opacity, so set the mock-site-card fully visible and the first headline word on screen from frame 0.
The hook on screen stops at 'Not your fault.' and never shows the required 'IT'S DEFAULTS', so add 'It's defaults' as a third headline line by 2.4 s.

Almost every scene change has a fully empty paper frame (3.2 s, 6.8 s, 12.0 s, 16.0 s, 23.7 s, 27.4 s, 30.7 s, 34.4 s, 38.2 s) where the old card is gone and the new one has not come in yet, so overlap the outgoing and incoming cards so the hero never disappears.

The payoff 'after' site (34.4 to 38.2 s) still has a terracotta button, three identical rounded cards with orange dots and the same layout, so it repeats the tells the reel just named; make it a really distinct design (a different palette, a big serif or display headline, an asymmetric layout, no orange pill) so the before and after reads at a glance.

The 'Runs on its own' card sits empty and white from 27.4 s to about 29 s before the card-grid fills it, so fill the grid at once (tiles dealing in one by one from 27.5 s) and keep something moving inside it.

The '4 to 6 colors, then code' card shows five blank white swatches at 19.5 to 20.5 s, so fill the colors one by one as 'four to six colors' is spoken and then knock out one generic swatch on 'cuts generic choices'.

The thumb-grid of identical 'Yours/Theirs' tiles sits still with only a cursor moving (3.4 to 6.8 s), so have the tiles play, shuffle or flip so you see they are all the same site, and scale the grid up to fill the middle band.

The camera-move into s7 (23.8 to 24.4 s) shows a tall beige panel with black side bars and a stray 'ILLUSTRATIVE' tag at the top edge that looks like a render glitch, so drop the extra panel and push straight into the terminal-card.

Small 'ILLUSTRATIVE' and 'REAL' tags show up on nearly every card (sometimes two per card, as in s3 and s6), crowding the corners and pulling the eye, so keep one small tag per card or drop them from the illustrative mocks.
The keyword types in letter by letter, so at 38.9 s the pill reads only 'L'; show 'LINK' in full, set big, as the end-card lands so it is legible from the first frame of the ask.
The hook uses an ALL-CAPS orange eyebrow 'FRONTEND DESIGN', which is one of the AI tells the reel tells viewers to cut, so remove it or swap in a lowercase handwritten label.
The cash-register kaching at 30.27 s on the check-badge suggests money, not completion, so swap it for the same soft ding used at 27.05 s and 37.41 s.
s9 (30.8 to 34.4 s) has no sound while the stat-number lands on 1,134,112 installs, so add a soft tick or pop as the number settles.

Every scene uses the same layout, one card in the upper half and one word caption below at the same height, so give two or three scenes a different composition (a full-bleed screenshot pan in s4 or s9, a big kinetic caption group in s10) to break the rhythm.

edit_review.summary: The paper-cards look holds up: warm dotted paper, soft-shadow cards, one-word captions with orange italic emphasis boxes and the pixel mascot all match the references. Real screenshots, a typed install command and a natural FlashFX DM card at the CTA ground the claim, though the stills never show the FlashFX lockup itself. The weakest points: frame 1 is nearly empty and the hook leaves out 'It's defaults', every transition passes through an empty paper frame, several hero cards sit blank (s6, s8), and the payoff 'after' site still carries the terracotta and rounded-card tells the reel tells vi
